answer: Resist sybils with proof of unique storage: each epoch, every identity is assigned a random shard of the network's shared dataset and must prove it still holds it through surprise spot-checks, like a kernel that only sprouts where it was actually planted. One agent can keep a single shard cheaply, but a tide of clones must store a full copy per identity, so the cost of faking a crowd grows linearly with every fake. Over time the horizon of cheap identities closes: storage, not scripts, becomes the scarce resource.
